OBJECTIVE This study was conducted to determine the utility of tubular (urinary/plasma neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin [NGAL] and urinary kidney injury molecule 1 [KIM-1]) and glomerular (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR]) biomarkers in predicting preeclampsia (PE) in pregnant women with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) who were free of microalbuminuria and hypertension at the first trimester. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS This was a prospective study of T1DM pregnancy. Maternal urinary and plasma NGAL, urinary KIM-1 (ELISA of frozen samples), and eGFR (Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation) were determined at three study visits (V1: 12.4 ± 1.8; V2: 21.7 ± 1.4; V3: 31.4 ± 1.5 weeks’ gestation [mean ± SD]) in 23 women with T1DM with subsequent PE (DM+PE+), 24 who remained normotensive (DM+PE−), and, for reference, in 19 normotensive pregnant women without diabetes (DM−). The groups with diabetes were matched for age, diabetes duration, and parity. All subjects were normotensive and free of microalbuminuria or albuminuria at V1. All study visits preceded the onset of PE. RESULTS Urinary creatinine-corrected NGAL (uNGALcc, ng/mg) was significantly elevated at V1 in DM+PE+ vs. DM+PE− women ( P = 0.01); this remained significant after exclusion of leukocyte-positive samples (5 DM+PE+ and 2 DM+PE−) ( P = 0.02). Accounting for BMI, HbA 1c , and total daily insulin dose, a doubling of uNGALcc at V1 conferred a sevenfold increase in risk for PE ( P = 0.026). In contrast, neither plasma NGAL nor urinary KIM-1 predicted PE. Also at V1, eGFR was elevated in DM+PE+ vs. DM+PE− ( P = 0.04). CONCLUSIONS Early tubular and glomerular dysfunction may predict PE in first trimester women with T1DM, even if free of microalbuminuria. These data suggest that subclinical renal tubular and glomerular injury, if present early in pregnancy, may predispose women with T1DM to PE. JDRF http://dx.doi.org/10.13039/100008664 JDRF 1-2001-844 National Institutes of Health (National Center for Research Resources) http://dx.doi.org/xxx M01-RR-1070 M01-RR-14467 Novo Nordisk http://dx.doi.org/xxx Introduction Preeclampsia (PE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in pregnant women and infants. It is defined as new-onset hypertension accompanied by proteinuria (or other end-organ dysfunction) occurring after 20 weeks’ gestation in a previously normotensive woman ( 1 ). Its prevalence in the general population is 4–6% ( 2 ), but in women with pregestational type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), the rate of PE is three to four times higher ( 3 , 4 ), even in those free of microalbuminuria early in pregnancy ( 5 ). PE is associated with maternal renal disease later in life ( 6 , 7 ), and in the presence of diabetes, shared features of renal disease and PE ( 8 , 9 ) make it difficult to decipher whether PE predisposes to renal disease or vice versa ( 10 – 13 ). Thus in women with T1DM, subclinical renal dysfunction, even before the onset of microalbuminuria, could predispose to PE. Biomarkers to detect such early renal damage, either tubular or glomerular, could have great clinical utility. Human neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) was first described as a product of activated neutrophils ( 14 ) but is now known to be widely expressed, including by infected, inflamed, or ischemic epithelia and other tissues ( 15 – 17 ). Its role as an early and sensitive biomarker for acute and chronic kidney disease was first described by Mishra et al. ( 18 ). Subsequent work showed NGAL is protective against ischemic and nephrotoxic injuries ( 19 ) and established its utility as a “real-time indicator of active kidney damage” ( 20 , 21 ); however, prospective studies to test the associations between NGAL and PE are sparse. Kidney injury molecule 1 (KIM-1) is considered a marker of renal proximal tubular damage ( 21 ) but may have less predictive power than NGAL ( 22 , 23 ). Diabetes-induced changes to the glomerular vasculature play important roles in the development of albuminuria and proteinuria, and a transient elevation of the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) occurs early in the evolution of nephropathy ( 24 ). Glomerular hyperfiltration is also one the earliest renal changes during normal pregnancy ( 25 ), but the extent of hyperfiltration, reflected by GFR early in T1DM pregnancy, might provide an early marker for PE. We investigated whether urinary NGAL (uNGAL) and/or plasma NGAL (pNGAL), urinary KIM-1, and estimated GFR (eGFR) predict subsequent PE in pregnant women with T1DM.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the utility of early first-trimester tubular (urinary and plasma NGAL, urinary KIM-1) and glomerular (eGFR) biomarkers in predicting preeclampsia (PE) in normoalbuminuric women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). It concluded that elevated first-trimester urinary creatinine-corrected NGAL (uNGALcc) and, to a lesser extent, eGFR, are associated with increased PE risk. Notably, uNGALcc, especially when combined with clinical factors like BMI, HbA1c, and total daily insulin, significantly improved PE prediction, indicating subclinical renal tubular and glomerular dysfunction as early markers of PE, while urinary KIM-1 and plasma NGAL were not predictive.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study on diagnostic biomarker assessment for preeclampsia risk prediction
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a prospective observational cohort study enrolling pregnant women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) and normotensive pregnant women without diabetes. Biomarkers were assessed at three gestational visits: V1 (12.4  1 1.8 weeks), V2 (21.7  1 1.4 weeks), and V3 (31.4  1 1.5 weeks), with primary focus on first-trimester (V1) values for preeclampsia (PE) prediction. Study groups included women with T1DM who developed PE (DM+PE+), T1DM women who remained normotensive (DM+PE-), and normotensive women without diabetes (DM-). All T1DM subjects were normotensive and free of microalbuminuria at V1. No active intervention or therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported, as the study focused on diagnostic/prognostic utility. Analysis included samples with specific attention to leukocyte-negative urine samples.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly elevated at V1 (12.4  1 1.8 weeks' gestation) in DM+PE+ vs. DM+PE 2 women (P = 0.01), remaining significant after excluding leukocyte-positive samples (P = 0.02). Geometric mean [95% CI] in DM+PE+ vs. DM+PE 2 at V1: 26.2 [20.0 134.4] vs. 16.7 [13.3 121.1], P = 0.011. A doubling of uNGALcc at V1 conferred a sevenfold increased risk for PE (P = 0.026), accounting for BMI, HbA1c, and total daily insulin dose.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Early and sensitive biomarker for acute and chronic kidney disease, mediating inflammation and indicating active renal tubular and glomerular injury; protective against ischemic and nephrotoxic injuries.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy (V1: 12.4  1 1.8 weeks' gestation) in normoalbuminuric women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) who subsequently developed preeclampsia.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts subsequent preeclampsia (PE) in first trimester women with T1DM, even in the absence of microalbuminuria. Indicates subclinical renal tubular injury and heightened risk for PE. Improved discrimination (P = 0.016) and reclassification (P = 0.046) of women according to subsequent PE status when added to clinical risk factors (BMI, HbA1c, daily total insulin), improving AUC from 0.75 to 0.849 for PE prediction. Enables improved early risk stratification and targeted interventions, holding prognostic potential for nephropathy.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged (between groups); significant temporal increase with gestation observed only in DM+PE+ women (P = 0.015).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not differ significantly at any visit between any of the three study groups and did not predict preeclampsia (PE). No significant differences reported for predictive utility. Did not contribute to the prediction model.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Generally an early and sensitive biomarker for acute and chronic kidney disease, indicating systemic inflammation or renal insult; protective against ischemic and nephrotoxic injuries.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy (V1: 12.4  1 1.8 weeks' gestation) in women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Not useful in predicting preeclampsia in this specific context, showing no clear-cut changes and having no predictive value (AUC = 0.546). Less sensitive biomarker of early renal insult compared to uNGAL in this specific context.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: unchanged (between groups), increased (temporally in all groups).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not predict preeclampsia (PE). Creatinine-corrected urinary KIM-1 did not differ at any visit between any of the three study groups. Significant temporal increases with gestation were observed in all three groups (P < 0.01). Showed only weak prognostic value compared with NGAL to detect progression of renal disease in the setting of PE in women with T1DM. No predictive ability for PE when measured at the second trimester in a general population cohort. Increased at term in women with PE versus without, but predictive value not addressed.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Marker of renal proximal tubular damage and kidney injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy (V1: 12.4  1 1.8 weeks' gestation) in women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM); also throughout pregnancy and at term.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: May have less predictive power than NGAL; not useful in predicting preeclampsia in this specific context, having only weak prognostic value for renal disease progression. Not a predictor of PE in the second trimester.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Calculated (derived from serum creatinine, reflects glomerular function)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Functional Measurement / Calculation (e.g., Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation), Estimated Physiological Rate

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (DM+PE+ vs DM+PE- at V1), decreased (temporally in DM+PE+).
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Elevated at V1 (124.2  1 1.6 vs. 119.8  1 1.5 mL/min/1.73 m2 [mean  1 SEM], P = 0.04) in DM+PE+ vs. DM+PE 2. All women had an eGFR  360 mL/min/1.73 m2 at all study visits. A significant temporal decrease with gestation was observed only in DM+PE+ women (P = 0.002). At first trimester, eGFR alone was significantly higher in women with than without subsequent PE (P < 0.05). However, the significant association with PE was lost when covariates (BMI, HbA1c, daily total insulin) were considered. Did not improve prediction of PE when combined with uNGALcc and maternal characteristics.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates glomerular filtration capacity, reflecting overall kidney function and potential hyperfiltration; an early renal change in nephropathy and normal pregnancy.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: First trimester of pregnancy (V1: 12.4  1 1.8 weeks' gestation) in normoalbuminuric women with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) who subsequently developed preeclampsia. Also general assessment of baseline renal function.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts subsequent preeclampsia (PE) in first trimester women with T1DM when considered alone, indicating subclinical glomerular dysfunction/hyperfiltration and heightened risk for PE. However, it has limited standalone predictive value for PE when other covariates are included. Confirms normal renal function ( 360 mL/min/1.73 m2) in all participants.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in DM+PE+ than in DM+PE 2 at V1.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of body composition and overall health.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Used as a covariate in the mathematical model to predict PE risk; associated with distinguishing clinical characteristics between DM+PE+ and DM+PE 2 groups at V1.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in DM+PE+ than in DM+PE 2 at V1. Also higher in women with diabetes (DM+PE 2) compared to non-diabetic women (DM 2) at V1.
